q:
Our almost 6 month old is waking every 45-60 minutes throughout the night, this has been the case since he was born. I’m losing my mind. He starts to stir, then escalates  
to crying. He is EBF, does not want my husband in the middle of the night. As soon as he’s in my arms he falls right back to sleep.
cx: Opening of the post; contact naps only by day.

q: Is anyone else struggling like this? I’m a shell of myself. I don’t do anything. I feel like the support group I was going to was a bragging group, everyone whining about 1-2 wake ups a night when we are up at least 6-8 times.
cx: Why she left her parents' support group.

q: I have tried everything, and often people seem to think we haven’t tried everything. Makes me feel like everyone thinks I’m a failure of my child is broken… it’s so hard.
cx: Replying to a sympathetic commenter.

q: I have tried to read precious little sleep, honestly struggle to do anything outside of work and trying to care for LO.
cx: A commenter suggested the Precious Little Sleep approach.

q: How do we put him down awake? We struggle so bad.
cx: After being told to put him down awake.

q: Do I just live the short nap life and try to make it to a reasonable bedtime every day and they will eventually lengthen again? Do I add a cat nap back in?
cx: 8.5 months, sleep trained; naps collapsed to 30 minutes this week.

q: yes maybe we need to be pushing wake windows a bit. I’ll try adding 15-30min and see how it goes!
cx: Taking a commenter's wake-window suggestion.

q: He is waking up from naps at 32 minutes on the dot no matter what. I’ve tried rouse to wake a few times - a few times he fully woke (oops), once he didn’t even stir, and once he stirred a little but stayed asleep until … 32 minutes. Only once did it help him get to 41 minutes. UGH.
cx: 11 months; trying the rouse-to-wake technique.

q: We are currently working on gentle sleep training and gradually having me fade away to get him to sleep more independently. We’re working with a sleep consultant too.
cx: Still asking the forum for nap tips while paying a consultant.

q: I keep blaming myself because I didn’t work on independent sleep from day one. I took the Taking Cara Babies newborn course and that stuff doesn’t work for him, read precious little sleep, Ferber book. I keep thinking maybe if I’d been more consistent, we wouldn’t be here.
cx: 3.5 months; contact naps since birth.

q: I spend hours every day trapped under a sleeping baby. I can’t make breakfast, drink my coffee while it’s hot, get work done, or even get up without worrying he’ll wake.
cx: The parent describes being completely burned out.

q: We’re planning to talk to our pediatrician at his 4-month appointment about sleep training, and I’m also meeting with a sleep consultant.
cx: After a course and two books did not work.

q:
Did your baby eventually learn to sleep independently?  
What method worked best?  
When did you start?  
Is there anything you wish you’d done differently before 4 months?  
If your baby only contact napped and struggled with the crib, what was the turning point?
cx: Asked of parents who had babies like theirs.

q: Is there a specific sleep training you did you recommend? I’m so lost on what to do. I’m thinking letting him fuss a bit from precious little sleep (def not CIO) to see when he’s 4 months old how he responds to that
cx: Follow-up to a commenter.

q: One of my friends recommended Ferber too and had great success. And from what I read in this sub it’s worked great for others too.
cx: Others' success stories shaping the parent's choice.

q: I know I’ll be crying too when we start ST & I’ll be just as shocked when (if) he sleeps on his own.
cx: Reacting to a commenter's success story.

q: she goes off to sleep around 8/9, sleeps solidly until about 11 and then she’s awake every 20 minutes
cx: Nearly 6 months; a month of this.

q: She’s having plenty of sleeps during the day, we use huckleberry for the sweet spot etc and we find it works for us.
cx: Uses the Huckleberry SweetSpot feature for naps.

q: maybe we need to be a bit more firm and leave her too it but it’s so hard when you’re so sleep deprived 🥲😂
cx: Asked whether they let her whine.

q: my grandparents live with us and they try to interfere/get upset when they hear her crying so it puts us in a bit of an awkward situation and we’ve tried to explain multiple times but might have to sit down with them again!
cx: Why letting her fuss is hard at home.

q: I’m back at work so she’s at nursery 2 days a week, my mum one day a week and my nana another day a week and then I’m home the rest of the time.
cx: Four different caregivers in a week; says they are not as consistent as they should be.

q: she’s still in our room as I said and will be for a very long time so it’s hard when they’re in the same room not to react I feel!
cx: On waiting before responding to wakings.

q: We did this 3 hour cap as per advice here as we were very undertired doing 2/2/2/2/2 with \~3.5/4hour of naps. Anyway. So we went back to 2/2/2/2/2 today and yesterday and it was just as bad. I don’t know what to do!
cx: Title: overtired with 3 naps, undertired with 2. Baby 5.5 months.

q: The 3 hour stretch to bed is mentally exhausting because there’s no settling him.
cx: The last wake window of the day.

q: The nights used to be 2.5 months of waking every 20-50 minutes. Now, he’s started doing much longer stretches.
cx: Context added in a reply.

q: I’m glad someone thinks we should sleep train now. I do think back a month ago and he wasn’t ready, but even though things aren’t perfect now I do think he will respond really well.
cx: Planning modified Ferber and a book a commenter named.

q: We used the Ferber method for my baby at 5 months. This girl never stopped crying for less than 20 minutes for 2-3 weeks straight. We eventually just rocked her to sleep, but she did learn how to self soothe throughout the night.
cx: Now 9 months; regression wakings.

q: It’s not ideal rocking her for every nap and bedtime, but I enjoy the cuddles and since she was sleeping great I didn’t want to mess with it.
cx: Why the rocking stayed.

q: I know this sleep association should’ve been taken away, but we didn’t. So how can we slowly move away from rocking to sleep at this point?
cx: Asks for a gradual route.

q: After trying the tape and black garbage bag method for a while, I’ve caved and bought sleepout curtains.
cx: 3.5 months; more sensitive to light and sound.

q: I’ve also seen some stuff about soft-close door mechanisms and under-the-door inserts to block light. Does anyone have solution or product Recommendations?
cx: Asking what else to buy.

q: I also fear that if I get him after he’s been crying for 30 minutes that it will become a routine for him, and he knows that he will get picked up after a certain amount of time. My question is, how long do I let him cry in there before giving up on a nap in total?
cx: 21 months, sleep trained at 8 months, suddenly screaming at naps.

q: I don’t really want to discuss wake windows because I cannot get her to nap on a schedule. I just have to follow her cues and even then it is a struggle.
cx: Six-month-old sleeping five hours a night.

q: Ferber resulted in crying the same amount of time every night for a week so we are taking a break
cx: Last line of the post.

q: I’ve been getting naps anyway I can and I’m sick of it. She naps 30 minutes on the dot in carrier, stroller, car seat, and contact. Ugh!!!
cx: Reply about naps.

q: Our pediatrician was not helpful at all and said “some babies just don’t sleep. At least she’s happy”. So we are going to a new pediatrician on the 14th.
cx: What the doctor said about very low total sleep.

q: Sigh. She has always slept less than the normal amount. I’m not an amazing sleeper but used to get 6 hours a night before baby.
cx: Reply to a commenter.

q: Oh yes, at this point I would take no naps and a 6 hour stretch at night if I could get it.
cx: Talking with another parent of a low-sleep baby.

q: I spent over a month chasing wake windows and I have never been so stressed, frustrated and sad thus far in my postpartum journey. Baby didn’t sleep either. She did her own thing, but I sure did a lot.
cx: Reply to another parent.

q: It is very isolating and I do get some negative comments particularly people focused on wake windows. I’ve even made a post about Windows to ensure that I’m doing it right. People truly do not understand and baby’s gonna do what baby wants to do. I’m right where you are now, radical acceptance.
cx: On the forum's wake-window replies.

q: Following precious little sleep sometimes and have to rescue the nap
cx: How she handles naps now.

q: Wow very helpful. This seems feasible.. I will try this starting today.. thank you very much
cx: Two days later, to a commenter's detailed plan.

q: WIth our eldest, we ferberized him and that worked super well. With this little nugget though, she goes from chill to hysterical withing seconds and she just doesn't come back from that.
cx: Almost 5 months; bedtime takes 19:00 to 21:30.

q: We're starting to dread nighttime as we know that one of us will have to sit with a screaming baby for 2 hours.
cx: Two weeks of hysterical bedtimes.

q: she was a velcro baby the first 11 weeks of her life and I was naptrapped most of the time
cx: Background; she had been improving.

q: I feel like she's overtired from her lack of naps but I can't make her sleep more if she refuses to do that...
cx: Naps of 20 minutes.

q: I thought it would get easier as time goes on (everyone says it does) but it doesn't feel like it's getting easier for me.
cx: 9 months; velcro baby from birth.

q: but even when my husband manages to get her down she usually wakes up shortly after looking for me anyway. So I prefer to put her to bed myself to save us all the trouble.
cx: Husband works long hours; no village.

q: I can't go anywhere without lugging diaper bags, stroller, carseat etc and having to worry constantly about wake windows and meal times and nap times and comforting her when she gets fussy in public.
cx: Why she rarely sees friends.

q: My relationship with my husband is the worse it's ever been and I'm so resentful that his life hasn't changed as much as mine has.
cx: Same post.

q: Basically, I want my life back.... everyone says things get better but I just can't see light at the end of the tunnel right now.
cx: Same post.

q: I go back to work in September also and I have no idea how we'll cope.... At the end of the day I know we will, but I feel so so guilty already and it sucks :(
cx: Replying to a commenter in the same situation.

q: My biggest question is… what do you all actually do with your babies for 3–4 hour wake windows?
cx: 9 months; still wakes multiple times a night.

q: I ended up introducing TV, which I know isn’t ideal at this age, but I was desperate.
cx: Too sleep deprived to fill long wake windows.

q: He’s never been a good sleeper and still wakes up multiple times every night, so by the next day I have no energy left. Maybe if I was actually getting some decent sleep, I’d find it easier to keep him entertained.
cx: Same post.

q: I know you're not meant to sleep train until at least 4mo and I likely won't even do it then, just putting that out there.
cx: Opening line; 9-week-old learning bassinet naps.

q: But because I'm right there is it bad? I'm literally right next to her with my hand on her chest. Am I doing damage? Is this considered sleep training?
cx: Baby cried 4 minutes in the bassinet with the parent beside her.

q: So her crying in the bassinet (with me 10cm away, hand on her chest) feels the same to me as her crying while strapped to me.
cx: She cries before contact naps too.

q: We started Ferber then switched to CIO (checks were making her cry more) at 4.5 months. After over a week, we were still having some nights where she cried for 30-45 minutes. I took advice on here and increased her daily awake time by 30 minutes, the next night she only cried for a minute. But that was short lived as crying increased again.
cx: 5 months; a free forum fix worked one night then wore off.

q: Some people on here said to take a break until she was a little older.
cx: What the forum told her next.

q: Do we start over with CIO? I don’t mind giving her the little extra help for now. I just don’t want her progress she’s made to be lost and start going backward.
cx: Now pats her to sleep; one feed a night.

q: She’s come a long way from cosleeping, nursing to sleep, waking every 2 hours, nightmare bedtimes, and false starts every night. So I’m really proud of the progress we’ve made but I know this isn’t independent sleep.
cx: Taking stock after the break.
